reason: The four cycle categories are disjoint and exhaustive relative to T=V(R): a cycle wholly on T either uses only R edges or at least one J edge; a cycle avoiding T lies in one connected component of G−T; every remaining cycle is mixed. For a mixed simple cycle, each maximal outside run lies in one actual G−T component and has two distinct boundary edges, while intervening T runs are paths in G[T]. The note handles a one-vertex outside run, equal T landings, and a trivial T run without treating an arbitrary concatenation as a simple cycle. Counting the two boundary edges per outside run gives its stated exact length sum, even if the same component occurs in several separate runs. A cycle with exactly one chord and otherwise R edges is precisely a previous chord-spectrum cycle; one outside run with its complementary T path in R is precisely a previous elementary return. Fan and original-pair markers count only physical edges, and selection supplies the inherited LengthOK exclusion. No exhaustive claim for the elementary spectra, target construction, multiplicity bound, rank charge, or closure is made.
